prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the organization of production areas and the material flow equipment used there.

learning_outcomes.text: Differentiate production logistics from the general logistics concept.
Illustrate modeling possibilities in production logistics and classify material planning activities.
Distinguish available technologies in the production logistics environment and explain planning processes for in-house material flow and logistics systems.
Explain the importance of in-house production logistics for the economical and sustainable production of products.
Integrate knowledge of key figures, models, and characteristic curves into planning work for in-house material flow and logistics systems.
Justify the choice of technologies to be used with regard to material movements and information flows.
Illustrate scope for action under economic and sustainability aspects.
Independently carry out projects within in-house production logistics.
Evaluate and use methods and tools for the analysis and planning of production logistics processes, integrating models - also using appropriate simulation tools - according to the state of the art.
Transfer the developed planning results to the operational environment and organize the necessary implementation work.

syllabus_topics: Tasks and goals of production logistics: logistics concept, in-house logistics, strategies, structures
Models of production logistics: product and process key figures, queuing model, logistical characteristic curves, characteristic curve theory
Material planning: inventory management, order quantity planning, administration systems
Technologies: storage and conveying systems, picking systems, identification systems, object tracking and localization, positioning systems, automation technologies

Planning of material flow and logistics systems: in-house transport, analysis of material flows, use of simulation, planning methods, layout planning (including planning methods) in the operational environment
Sustainability in production logistics: holistic considerations of strategies and systems, environmentally and resource-friendly processes and operating resources, scope for action, economic aspects
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is determined by the lecturer: either a written exam or a written project report. For the written exam, the duration is according to the valid study regulations. The project report should be 15-20 pages. The ungraded experimental work consists of 2 to 4 experimental tasks.
